notes.title: The WOMEN WANT ME Expansion is coming SEPTEMBER 25TH!!
notes.content: [h1]RISE, COSMIC DEBTORS.[/h1][h2]YOUR DESTINY REACHES OUT TO YOU FROM THE DEEP.[/h2][h2]YOU HEAR THE ECHOES OF A NAME.[/h2][h2]YOUR NAME.[/h2][h1]KINGFISHER.[/h1][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/2125ae8064bfa0cb69fe9514432cfe529b8215c8.gif"][/img][/p][p]I'm delighted to report that [b]the free[/b] [b]WOMEN WANT ME content expansion is coming out September 25th!![/b] This expansion will feature:[/p][list][*][p]A new map (The Lake of the Lady)[/p][/*][*][p]75+ new fish[/p][/*][*][p]Several new boats and weapons[/p][/*][*][p]4+ metaprogression upgrades to help make the early game more interesting[/p][/*][*][p]New late-game challenges for experienced players to pursue[/p][/*][*][p]Lots of secrets and esoteric mechanics[/p][/*][*][p]A new storyline with animated cutscenes[/p][/*][*][p]A new fully-voiced music track by Josie Brechner and dloot[/p][/*][*][p]Whatever's going on here:[/p][/*][/list][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/2950060f71aa2d22461b8432bd38e62a7bfd9f20.gif"][/img][/p][p]I'm really excited to put this expansion out! As previously mentioned, it'll be [b]completely free!![/b] You won't have to pay an extra cent to get the new content.[/p][p]And, speaking of cents...[/p][h1]NEW UPCOMING GAME: UNFAIR FLIPS[/h1][p]I'm excited to report that I've got a new game in the works!![/p][p][dynamiclink href="https://store.steampowered.com/app/3925760/Unfair_Flips/"][/dynamiclink][b]Unfair Flips is an incremental clicker game[/b] about flipping the world's worst coin over and over until you get [b]ten heads in a row.[/b] It's an [b]exercise in pure probability:[/b] every coin flip is completely random according to the current percentage chances given. It's entirely possible to win this game immediately by getting extremely lucky, but it's just as possible that the game never lets you land heads at all. There is no guarantee other than time.[/p][p]As you can see, [b]Unfair Flips is ALSO launching on September 25th!![/b] I decided to launch two games on the same day because I love suffering.[/p][previewyoutube="S69eCfQ4WQE;full"][/previewyoutube][p]This is just a little thing -- it exists in the GET RICH AND DIE TRYING universe (i.e. Goose's cousin Gar is there), but it's mechanically very different from SNAKE FARM and FISH FEAR ME. I had an idea for a weird little project and it basically fell together fully-formed. I'm pretty happy with how it's turned out![/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/a38ee9c714cbd7ebdd56690183ceefbb747381fe.gif"][/img][/p][p]It features art by Gwyndolyn Marchant, the guest artist for the WOMEN WANT ME expansion of FISH FEAR ME! (She drew that sword up there, and a few other things.) It also features a guest sound effect by Surasshu -- you'll know it when you hear it.[/p][p]September 25th is gonna be a really big day!! For these reasons, and also some secret other ones!!! I'm really looking forward to it!!!![/p][h1]Question of the week[/h1][p]What's the luckiest you've ever been?[/p][p][/p][p]Happy fishing,[/p][p]Heather Flowers[/p]

notes.title: Patch notes 5/9/2025: Full Controller Support!!
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] FISH FEAR ME Friday brings with it a bounteous tide this week: [b]the controller support update is now live!![/b] Let's dive into it!

[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Added controller navigation support to the entire game![/b] All UI elements can now be interacted with via controller. You can play the entire game without once touching the keyboard or mouse!
[*]Similarly, [b]beefed up support for mouse and keyboard players.[/b] You can finally use the scroll wheel to select bait, or use the keyboard to navigate UI menus!
[*]Updated the key binding menu backend to support a much more robust interaction system. The result of this is that [b]more control rebinding options are available.[/b] Try it out!
[/list]Huge shoutouts to visiting programmer Noé Charron for pinch hitting this update. Seriously, this would NOT have been possible without them. Everyone say "Thank you Noé!"

This update involved a LOT of backend changes, so PLEASE let us know in the Steam forums if you notice anything awkward or awry. We're determined to make it so every player has the best experience possible!

[h1]Question of the Week[/h1]
Uhhhhh fish?? How about em??? (It's been a long week.)

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

notes.title: The Controller Support Beta is now live!
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] Welcome to FISH FEAR ME Friday! I, your humble captain of the post-apocalyptic waves, come to you with a new public beta!

[h1]THE CONTROLLER SUPPORT BETA[/h1]
Over the past several weeks, visiting programmer Noé Charron has been working hard on getting full controller support for the game up and running. I'm excited to report that this project is now complete and ready for beta testing! We want to make sure it's good and solid before pushing it to main, so that everyone has the best experience with the game possible.

[h2]BETA CHANGE NOTES[/h2]
[list]
[*] [b]Added controller navigation support to the entire game![/b] All UI elements can now be interacted with via controller. You can play the entire game without once touching the keyboard or mouse!
[*] Similarly, [b]beefed up support for mouse and keyboard players.[/b] You can finally use the scroll wheel to select bait, or use the keyboard to navigate UI menus!
[*] [b]Updated the key binding menu backend[/b] to support a much more robust interaction system. The result of this is that more control rebinding options are available. Try it out!
[/list]
[h2]TO ACCESS THE CONTROLLER SUPPORT BETA:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Right-click FISH FEAR ME in your Steam library
[*] Go to Properties->Betas
[*] Type in the code ControllerTest
[*] Opt into the beta
[*] Update your game
[*] Have fun!
[/list]
Of note: [b]participating in the beta will not alter your save in any way![/b] 

Controller players, be sure to let us know what you think! And non-controller players, please do the same! We're trying to make sure that [i]everyone[/i] has the best possible experience with this update. The best place to give feedback is in the Suggestions and Bug Reporting threads:

https://steamcommunity.com/app/3000120/discussions/0/594016102539910965/

https://steamcommunity.com/app/3000120/discussions/0/594016102539910793/


If all goes well, we'll be pushing controller support to the main game very soon!

[h1]Question of the Week[/h1]
The eldritch goddess RAMONA appears in both FISH FEAR ME and SNAKE FARM. But do you know where the character that inspired her namesake [i]originally[/i] comes from?

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

notes.title: FISH FEAR ME Friday 4/18/2025 - Controller Progress Update!
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] The fish are chasing me, and they're humming a new tune. It's FISH FEAR ME Friday!

[b]This week:[/b] Progress updates on [b]the controller support update[/b] and [b]the free WOMEN WANT ME expansion![/b]

[h1]Controller Progress Update[/h1]
I'm excited to report that [b]the controller support update is nearly complete!![/b] Visiting programmer Noé Charron and I have been working together today to start putting together the finishing touches and hammer out the last couple bugs.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/835d0349f74ba664ff294f8a72263f527b5bc064.png[/img]
[i]Look! Controller button prompts and everything!![/i]

This has taken a fair bit of work because [i]a certain someone[/i] (me) didn't listen when [i]a certain someone else[/i] (literally everybody I talked to) told me to build out this UI with controllers in mind in the first place. Retrofitting it is a lot more work than just doing it right the first time, it turns out!! Lesson learned!!!

Anyways, the controller update should be ready for beta testing soon, and ready for public consumption soon after! Thank you all for your patience!

[h1]WOMEN WANT ME Progress Update[/h1]
Something very key to FISH FEAR ME's charm, in my opinion, is its use of live instrumentation and singers in its music tracks. I've talked a lot about the upcoming new track, KINGFISHER, over the past few weeks -- let's talk a little about what it takes to put together a track like this!

[previewyoutube=-MP-VMCDv6A;full][/previewyoutube]
[i]Above: legendary bassist Audrey Zee Whitesides absolutely shredding.[/i]

The first step of the process is between me and Josie Brechner, the project's composer, where we hammer out the themes and vibes of the track. This is usually a meeting where I ask "can we have it be, like, sorta witch rock, but also kinda power metal, but also it's all medieval themed so there's a lute? Here's a bunch of lore on the character this song's about. Could we incorporate this, somehow? And also maybe a monastic style melody, but it's still rock?" and Josie miraculously interprets this as a coherent train of thought. Then, I write up some lyrics and send them over, she works out a melody, and the work begins in proper!

The track then goes through a ton of iterations as we both play with various ideas. What if the lyrics were in iambic pentameter? What if we added a chorus here? What if there was an organ playing in the background at points? Once the structure of the song is solid and we're both happy with it, Josie's able to bring live musicians into the studio to make the piece, well, [i]sing.[/i]

[previewyoutube=FukrsqxT0V4;full][/previewyoutube]
[i]Above: dloot, the vocalist for the FISH FEAR ME theme, returns to the studio for KINGFISHER.[/i]

Once the live sessions have been completed, all that's left is final mixing and polish! Much like the FISH FEAR ME theme, this song has an instrumental version that plays during gameplay and a vocal version that plays during special in-game circumstances; this is the part of the process where both pieces are finalized at once. Both pieces are put in-game, and the expansion gets one step closer to completion!

[h1]Question of the Week[/h1]
What's a video game song that [i]you[/i] never get tired of listening to?

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

notes.title: FISH FEAR ME Friday 4/11/2025 - Catching the Leviathan
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] Tides rise, the moon falls, and FISH FEAR ME Friday returns gently once more.

Today, I wanted to talk about everyone's favorite eldritch monstrosity, the Leviathan! Making a satisfying ending to a roguelike presents interesting challenges for design, programming, and narrative, so let's dive right in!

[b]Spoilers abound[/b] for the end of the game, so beware!!

[h1]Designing the Leviathan[/h1]
From very early on, I wanted FISH FEAR ME to have a strong finish to its "main storyline." The obvious comparison point is the Reaper from Vampire Survivors: you've reached the time limit, which means it's time to die! Overcoming this barrier (and meeting the [i]actual[/i] endpoint of the run) is the final challenge of the main campaign, so it's important that it shines.

The design for the Reaper is interesting to me for a few reasons. First is the fact that it can be done in [i]any[/i] run once you reach a certain point. All the items you need are available on every map; all you have to do is take the time to walk to them (and accept their downsides/challenges). This is a very core principle which I wanted to uphold while making FISH FEAR ME. Preparing to fight the Leviathan may be a significant undertaking, but it's doable in every map once you've unlocked the Bell of the Deep and Ghost Knife.

However, where our design sensibilities differed is that I wanted the Leviathan to be a unique fight for each map. An original design for the game had a [i]completely[/i] different encounter for each map: a kraken for Shipwreck Bay, a horde of fish for Nightmare Lake, etc. It would've been a cool idea, but a significant chunk of work (and it would've somewhat dampened the impact of the fight, being with [i]A Leviathan[/i] rather than [i]The Leviathan[/i]). In the end, I made it so that the Leviathan summons guardian fish from your current map and forces you to fight them, making each fight substantially different while maintaining the unique character of each map!

[h1]Programming the Leviathan[/h1]
FISH FEAR ME is a game with a wide variety of player builds, which means it's very difficult to know what setup the player is going to have when they reach the Leviathan fight. All I can know is that they're strong enough to complete all five altar rituals. Can they deal fifty damage per second? Five thousand? I don't know!

Therefore, the Leviathan boss fight must be winnable by all types of endgame build: if you have high DPS, you can gun it down (but not too fast). If you have high health, you can outlive it (at a high risk). If you summon the undead, there are undead for you to summon (but not an infinite amount). Eventually, the following design decisions were reached:
[list]
[*][b]The Leviathan itself has relatively low health, but regularly becomes invincible.[/b] This way, high-DPS builds are rewarded but can't completely curbstomp it, and low-DPS builds can make decent progress.
[*][b]To end these invincibility periods, you need to either kill all summoned guardian fish OR survive for 45 seconds.[/b] Again, multiple solutions! A good survival build can make it through the 45-second maximum no problem, while the DPS build can chew through the spawned enemies.
[*][b]When the clock strikes midnight, ALL fish spawning pools are refilled.[/b] Even if you fished out the entirety of Nightmare Lake on Day 7, there are still new fish for you to catch during the fight. This way, you're given ample opportunities to heal (and summon skeletal minions) while battling the Leviathan!
[/list]
[h1]Writing the Leviathan[/h1]
"Writing" is an interesting word given the low word count of the game, but I do generally try to keep an internal sense of logic: why things happen, why things happen [i]again[/i], etc. The biggest question every roguelike invites writing-wise is "Why does this keep happening?" Why does the Fisherman keep fishing after he dies? Why can you fight the Leviathan multiple times? Why does paying off the life debt [spoiler]not end the game[/spoiler]?

The world of FISH FEAR ME is one of cosmic loops: death and undeath, debt and undebt. "As above, so below, so further, so above." The relationship between the Leviathan and the Fisherman is one of these loops: we live, we fish, we die, we fish again. The two are permanently connected. Even when you slay the Leviathan, it gets its revenge.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/abb1dbdc122f326731fd103605bccce8e376dff9.png[/img]

That's all for this week! Thank you for reading, and I'll see you next week for [b]another FISH FEAR ME Friday![/b]

[h1]Question of the Week[/h1]
What are some of [i]your[/i] favorite bosses in roguelikes/survivorslikes?

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

notes.title: FISH FEAR ME Friday 4/4/2025 - Discounts and Viscounts
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] The tides rise, the tides fall, and FISH FEAR ME Friday returns to us once more.

[h1]Discounts![/h1]

Two exciting pieces of news:

First, [b]FISH FEAR ME is now in a bundle with Genome Guardian![/b] For those not aware, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2891310/Genome_Guardian/]Genome Guardian[/url] is a roguelite turret shooter where you fight off cells while mutating your weaponry with DNA. It's a very cool game -- check it out!

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/45393/_Genome_Guardian_x_FISH_FEAR_ME__Roguelike_Duo/

Second, [b]FISH FEAR ME will be going on sale on April 7th![/b] This will be the game's first post-launch sale, at 20% off. Tell your friends if you think they'd like it! (Or your enemies, if you think they wouldn't????)

[h1]Viscounts![/h1]

This past week, we got [url=https://dloot.bandcamp.com]Dloot[/url] (the lead singer on the FISH FEAR ME title track) back in the studio to record lyrics for the new song in the [b]upcoming free WOMEN WANT ME content expansion![/b] The new song is an extreme bop: I've had the chorus stuck in my head ever since I first heard it. The song, KINGFISHER, tells the woeful tale of the Lady of the Lake: her history, her bleak fate, and her murderous intent towards the Fisherman. Or, to quote the chorus directly:

[i]KINGFISHER, TAKE UP THE SWORD
KINGFISHER, WEAR THE CROWN
KINGFISHER, THIS ALL COULD BE YOURS
GRAB YOUR FATE OR DROWN[/i]

[h1]Question of the Week[/h1]
Is fate the result of human action or human inaction? Is the future as set in stone as the past?

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

notes.title: Patch notes 3/28/2025
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] We have sailed once again to FISH FEAR ME Friday!

Just a quick patch notes this week -- there's a lot of behind-the-scenes work going into the upcoming free content expansion, so that's where the majority of our dev time is currently pointed. As always, changes marked with ⚓ are community suggestions!

[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
[h2]Misc[/h2]
[list]
[*]⚓ Added the ability to pause during [spoiler]the Leviathan fight[/spoiler]
[/list][h1]Controller Navigation[/h1]
In exciting news, controller navigation has made huge steps forward in the past couple weeks! Every screen requires a bespoke UI solution, so it'll still be a while before this update is ready to make public, but it's VERY cool to see in progress. Here's several menu screens, all being navigated entirely with the controller!!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/6f42d6facc6b6cc52b485f0e2bf31c9237bfc05f.gif[/img]

I've said it before and I'll say it again: Noé, our visiting programmer, is a genius.

[h1]Women Want Me[/h1]
The [b]upcoming free content expansion,[/b] WOMEN WANT ME, is continuing apace! I've gotten the level design solidified and have started implementing it in-engine -- I can't show you that, of course, but I'll give you some facts about the area:

[h1]Question of the Week[/h1]
What item do you always take whenever it shows up? What item do you never take?

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

notes.title: Patch notes 3/21/2025
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] We have once again made it to FISH FEAR ME Friday!

First, patch notes! As always, patch notes marked with ⚓ are community suggestions.

[h1]Patch Notes[/h1]
[h2]Game Balance[/h2]
[list]
[*]⚓ [b]Significantly buffed money-making weapons:[/b]
[*][b]Party Cannon:[/b] $1/shot -> $5/shot
[*][b]Ritual of Pain:[/b] Changed money gained per ritual from $5 to $10 (LVL 1-2), from $5 to $25 (LVL 3), and from $10 to $50 (LVL 4-6)
[*][b]Metal Detector:[/b] Changed like so:
LVL 1: $1 per overheal, max $25 -> $1 per overheal, max $50
LVL 2: $1 per overheal, max $50 -> $2 per overheal, max $75
LVL 3: $1 per overheal, max $100 -> $2 per overheal, max $100
LVL 4: $2 per overheal, max $200 -> $4 per overheal, max $200
LVL 5: $3 per overheal, max $500 -> $6 per overheal, max $500
LVL 6: $3 per overheal, no max -> $10 per overheal, no max
[/list]Money-making weapons were broadly underpowered as a category, given their high opportunity cost and low reward. The idea in buffing them like this is to make them more viable in the early-game and provide a stronger risk-reward profile: here's a way of getting significant extra money on top of your fishing, but you miss out on getting a more combat-viable weapon in that slot.
[h2]Bugfixes/Misc[/h2]
[list]
[*]⚓Fixed a bug where Metal Detector + Summoning Ritual would produce extremely loud noises when triggered simultaneously
[*]Fixed a bug where damage numbers were showing up as the wrong color
[*][b]Optimization:[/b] Changed fish and projectile physics from dynamic to kinematic
[*][b]Optimization:[/b] Made squids spawn trails slightly less often
[/list]The dynamic->kinematic change should ideally have zero effect on gameplay but decently improve performance. If you notice anything behaving strangely (like its physics is "wrong" for whatever reason) let us know -- this is probably why!

[h1]Upcoming Content[/h1]
[h2]Optimization and Usability[/h2]
Visiting programmer Noé has been hard at work recently doing controller UI navigation, and it's starting to show results! This game has a [i]lot[/i] of menus, and each one requires a semi-bespoke solution, so it's a bit of a Herculean task. Still, progress is being made!!

[h2]WOMEN WANT ME[/h2]
Work on the WOMEN WANT ME expansion is going well! I recently spent a day jamming with Josie Brechner, the game's composer, as we figured out the arc of the expansion's new song. The song's name is [b]KINGFISHER,[/b] and it's both a tragic tale of the Lady of the Lake's eternal solitude and an absolute banger. I've been listening to a WIP version of the track on loop all morning -- it's [i]really[/i] good.

As some of you know, when I work on content expansions for games, I usually start by setting up a few new mechanics to play with, and then putting them through their paces. For SNAKE FARM: THE CURSE OF RAMONA, this was bomb attacks and teleporting snakes; for WOMEN WANT ME, I'm starting out by creating some new fish AI patterns!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/88531f607b6eef352065eef247335f79eebc01e9.gif[/img]

This stop-and-start pattern is useful in a few different contexts -- here, it creates a swarm of lizards that aim and pounce, but it can also be used for the Mimic Octopus I posted about a couple weeks ago:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/165c4891941e302f1cb72c56c16b83c38be4110b.gif[/img]

Get ready to never trust a bounty again :)

[h1]Community Spotlight[/h1]
I'm excited to report that [b]FISH FEAR ME has its first mod!![/b] [i]Sea Sick Me[/i] by SilverQueenRuby is a mod that rotates the camera alongside the boat, de-centers the boat and UI, gives physics to UI elements, and adds screenshake when you're hit. I'm not adding a gif to demonstrate, because [b]I genuinely cannot play this mod for more than thirty seconds without feeling physically ill.[/b] It's a delight.

Check it out!

https://www.nexusmods.com/fishfearme/mods/1

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/90ad37c602453873311f56dc0979bcfa91ac1e20.png[/img]

[h1]Question of the Week[/h1]
What's your favorite fish?

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

notes.title: FISH FEAR ME Friday - 3/14/2025
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] Welcome to yet another FISH FEAR ME Friday!

No patch notes today! We're currently working on some longer-term goals, so it might be a bit before they're ready to push. Still, I'm here to tell you all about all the news in the cosmic sea!

[h1]Optimization and Usability[/h1]
As you might know, recently I brought on visiting programmer Noé Charron to work on [b]performance optimization[/b] with fantastic results. They've also started working on [b]controller UI navigation![/b] Much like optimization, this is a long process with a lot of fiddly bits, so it may be a bit before it's complete. I'm very much looking forward to it, though -- with a little time and a lot of work, soon the entire game will be playable with a controller!

[h1]Women Want Me[/h1]
Preproduction for [b]the free WOMEN WANT ME expansion[/b] is still going well! This stage involves creating a lot of .txt files I call wishlists -- what the expansion [i]would[/i] include if I had infinite time and money. I usually end up making it through about 80% of these items and scrapping the remaining 20%.

notes.title: Patch notes 3/7/2025
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b] It is once again FISH FEAR ME Friday!

Let's jump right in with the patch notes. As always, notes tagged with ⚓ are community suggestions!

[h1]PATCH NOTES[/h1]
[h2]Balance changes[/h2]
[list]
[*]⚓ [b]Buffed Cursed Crown:[/b] now, instead of the curse being that you're stuck at 1hp forever, it's that you can no longer heal. This is still a very significant downside, but it should [i]hopefully[/i] provide build niche opportunities outside of Ghost Ship runs.
[*]⚓ Added [b]triple invincibility duration[/b] on expending a [spoiler]Stitched Heart[/spoiler]
[*][b]Accidentally nerfed and then partially buffed Chum.[/b] So it turns out that Chum was actually getting called twice per fish summon initialization, which meant that it was [i]significantly[/i] stronger than intended when combined with Ichthyomancy, Dragon Tooth, or Tamed Shark. I fixed the double call to rein in the balance more towards what I'd intended... and then gave it a more intentional buff so it'd stay competitive in the meta. It's weaker than it was, but stronger than it was originally supposed to be!
[*]Improved fish summon AI
[/list][h2]Bugfixes[/h2]
[list]
[*]⚓ Fixed a bug where the Trawler and Party Boat would show missing day 4 unlocks
[*]⚓ Fixed a bug where using the [spoiler]Bell of the Deep[/spoiler] would consume junk fish lots, causing the spawn pool to deplete prematurely
[/list][h2]Misc[/h2]
[list]
[*]⚓ [b]Changed the sprite for Moonwater Lure[/b] to make it more apparent when it's been unlocked (and cuter)
[*][b]Made the "continuous hold" fishing minigame the default.[/b] I'm keeping classic mode in the options menu for the real sickos, but it's very apparent that this new version is strongly preferred by pretty much everyone. I'll be doing some UI changes on it soon to make it more visually clear what's going on, but the long and short is you can hold down the spacebar forever now to just continually summon new fish!
[*]Did a [b]gigantic optimization pass[/b] on pretty much the entire game.
[/list]
I want to talk a bit about this optimization pass. As I mentioned in the last newspost, I brought in visiting programmer (and absolute genius) Noé Charron to help fix some of the lag spikes the game was having, and they REALLY delivered. To showcase this, I ran a benchmark on my old Thinkpad, with the build the community's started calling "the lag bomb" (Ichthyomancy/Cursed Crown/Absolute Violence/Summoning Ritual). Here it is with last week's build...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/e59cf22fabc178224f28cdfd058cf26dc624af82.jpg[/img]
[i](VAR is short for Framerate Variance; basically the distance between the longest and shortest frames in the past 60 frames. High VAR means a huge lag spike has just happened.)[/i]

And with this week's build.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/9921b1038e3ec3b4769cc900967f3b1c88e0ef3c.jpg[/img]

Long story short, Noé's a miracle worker.

Now, there's two things to discuss with optimization. First off, [b]this is a continuous process.[/b] There are still parts of the game that need optimizing, and I'll be partly relying on y'all to point out specific circumstances that cause lag spikes! I'm already aware of one element that still needs fixing (squid trails are a huge lag culprit at the moment), but I'm sure there's other elements that I haven't spotted yet because I'm just one person.

Second off, optimization can introduce some really [i]subtle[/i] bugs. The way that optimization works is you take a previously-flexible part of the game and make it more rigid by encoding some gameplay assumptions as fundamental rules. Stuff like "attacks will never change size over their lifetimes" or "fish all have the same set of components." Then, you suddenly remember an edge case to that, and then an edge case to the edge case, and now you have a bunch of tiny changes to game logic where things don't work [i]quite[/i] like they're supposed to. I've gone through and already fixed a fair few of these bugs, but it's a near-inevitability that I've missed something because -- again -- I'm just one person!

So, with both those in mind, if you notice anything odd about the game over the next week or two, [b]please let us know![/b] Community manager Hearth has put together [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3000120/discussions/0/594016102539910793/]a bug reports thread[/url] in the Forum for your convenience.

Now, [b]on to the future![/b] My current plans include:
[list]
[*]Continuing to work on [b]optimization[/b]
[*]Continuing to work on [b]usability[/b]
[*]Giving the new [b]fishing minigame[/b] a more unique look
[*]Making [b]controller support[/b] a lot more functional (this one's a bit of a bear to fix, but I promise it's on my list)
[*]Starting production on [b]the free WOMEN WANT ME expansion[/b]
[/list]
Actually, on the topic of WOMEN WANT ME, I've got two pieces of news!

First off, I'm excited to announce that Josie Brechner will be returning to make another song for the expansion! Josie's the composer for the base game, and I think we can all agree her music is one of the best things about it. The new track doesn't have a name yet, but I can already tell you it's gonna be a great one.

Second off, I want to highlight one of the new fish I'm working on for the expansion! Say hello to the Lake of the Lady's stealthiest occupant, the Mimic Octopus...

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/f6111f7e6a8f5d28836742f19897709ef787e52f.png[/img]

[h1]Question of the Week[/h1]
What do you most want to see in a new map?

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

P.S. Here's the new sprite for the Moonwater lure! As is indie dev tradition, both it and the [spoiler]Moonbeam Catfish[/spoiler] are based off my real-life cat.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/18913bbf485b363c4a4eda46e93362c0287d4f6f.png[/img]

It's been one week since launch and I'm slowly starting to exist on this planet again. Today, I've got a patch for y'all and a couple announcements!

[h1]PATCH NOTES[/h1]

[list]
[*]⚓ [b][EXPERIMENTAL][/b] Added an alternate version of the fishing minigame which allows you to spawn more fish by just continuously holding the FISH button. To activate it, look in the Options menu!

[*]⚓ Fixed a bug where swapping bait partway through the fishing minigame would cause the wrong type of bait to be expended

[*]Fixed a major performance hitch when succeeding at the fishing minigame
[*]Fixed a bug where every boat's destruction animation briefly turned it into the rowboat

If you try out the alternate version of the fishing minigame, be sure to let us know how it goes! Big changes to fundamental systems like this are always a little tricky, so [b]this alternate mode is very liable to change over the next couple weeks.[/b]

Additionally, I'm excited to report that the project has a couple new faces! You may have already seen Hearth, our new community manager, in the forums, but here's her self-introduction:

[i]Hello everyone!

My name's Hearth, and my pronouns are She/Her. I've agreed to help Heather in organizing the bug reports and feedback you've all been submitting! You can think of me as your courier dragon, compiling and taking all your input to Heather for them to address.

I'll also be moderating in case any discussions here get too out of hand, but from what I've seen y'all are pretty well-behaved.

I'm here to help, so feel free to poke me with anything you've got! I hope you're all enjoying what Heather put together here, and I'll see you around!

-Hearth[/i]

She's already been helping out massively with the project, making sure the forums are organized and nobody's feedback slips through the cracks. And yes, fish [i]do[/i] fear her -- she's been a playtester since day one!

Additionally, visiting programmer Noé Charron is going to be [b]helping out with performance optimization[/b] over the next couple weeks. The performance fix in the patch notes is something they spotted immediately upon touring the project, and it's the first of many improvements to come! Next steps will involve completely retooling the fish and attack scripts to use object pooling, which should solve a LOT of lag issues once completed.

Finally, preparations for the next [b]free content expansion,[/b] WOMEN WANT ME, are continuing apace. I can't share much yet, but I should have more news very soon! The Lake of the Lady calls...

notes.title: Post-Launch Development Roadmap
notes.content:
[b]Ahoy, cosmic debtors![/b]

First of all, I want to thank each and every one of you for a tremendously successful launch. These past few days have been an absolute whirlwind of excitement -- did you know we've been on the New and Trending list for three entire days? I'm still barely on this planet. To every single person who played the game, or wishlisted it, or posted their thoughts on it: [b]thank you, thank you, thank you.[/b]

So, with that in mind, let's talk about the future! I'm not planning on resting on my laurels here. Y'all have shown that there's a genuine desire for this game, and so I want to continue making it the best that it can be. This boils down to three things: [b]optimization, usability, and content.[/b]

[h2]OPTIMIZATION[/h2]
I've heard the reports that the game doesn't run as well as it could -- I'll fully admit I'm not the best programmer when it comes to optimization, which is why I'm [b]bringing in a more experienced programmer to help.[/b] They'll be looking over the codebase over the next week or two, noting any and all possible performance improvements, and I'll be making as many of them as possible. With a little luck and a lot of work, the game should be [b]running much more smoothly soon![/b]

[h2]USABILITY[/h2]
I want to thank everyone who's been posting their thoughts in the forum about parts of the game that are unclear or don't work as expected! I'll be [b]fixing as many of those issues as possible[/b] over the next few weeks, and rounding out some of the game's systems to better answer some of the questions that keep coming up (e.g. "where the hell is the Red Herring"). This may be a little patchwork over time -- certain things that seem easy are actually extremely difficult, and certain other things that seem difficult are surprisingly easy. [b]I fully intend to get to everything,[/b] but it might take a while.

[h2]CONTENT[/h2]
[b]As it stands, the game is a complete experience.[/b] It sets out a series of premises -- the life debt, the Leviathan, the book of forbidden knowledge, the multiple maps -- and fully explores each and every one of them by the end of its runtime. I wouldn't have launched the game if I felt it was incomplete! But that doesn't mean there can't be [i]more[/i] to the story.

So, with that in mind, I want to announce my plans for [b]the first free content update to FISH FEAR ME![/b] It's still very early in its planning stage (I don't even have an [i]idea[/i] of a release date yet), but I want to give you a taste.

[i]You awaken in the middle of the night as your boat lurches. "Rise," a voice calls from the lake, and you do. You step onto the deck of your ship, gazing out at the reflection of the shattered moon on the water. The light coalesces into a figure beneath the surface: glowing, ethereal, feminine.[/i]

[i]The Lady rises into the air, and as she does, you notice something trailing behind her. A long, metallic object: the only part of her that seems remotely real. "I wish to give you something," she says, holding the sword aloft. It lifts from her hands, suspended in moonlight, dripping and weighty.[/i]

[i]In an instant, the sword points at you, flying forwards. No time to react. It pierces your heart and you fall. As you succumb once more to the Deep, the Lady whispers one more thing: "If you wish to prove your worthiness, find me again..."[/i]

[b]Announcing the first free expansion to FISH FEAR ME...[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45120257/a1f6026b2521e94f0ac8f98997692493ac632c7a.png[/img]

[b]FISH FEAR ME: WOMEN WANT ME[/b] will focus on [b]a new map,[/b] the Lake of the Lady, and its supernatural inhabitants. It will feature [b]new upgrades, new weapons, new boats, new fish,[/b] and [b]new gameplay mechanics.[/b] If I do my job right, it'll provide both new content for new players and a new challenge for experienced players to overcome!

As previously mentioned, [b]this will be a free content update, available to everyone who owns the game.[/b] I'm not certain when exactly it'll come out, but I'll keep y'all updated on its progress!!

That's all for this time! I have even more plans once all this is done, but I don't want to overwhelm y'all. Thank you for reading, and thank you for playing FISH FEAR ME!

Happy fishing,
Heather Flowers

notes.title: FISH FEAR ME is coming out FEBRUARY 21st!!
notes.content:
I'm incredibly excited to announce that [b]FISH FEAR ME will be coming out February 21st!![/b] Wishlist it now to get notified when the game launches:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3000120/FISH_FEAR_ME/

MORE DETAILS:
[list]
[*] The game will be launching [b]on February 21st for $9.99, with a 20% discount for the first two weeks (so $7.99 in practice).[/b]
[*] It features [b]three maps, fifteen biomes, sixteen boats, thirty weapons, and 150ish fish to catch.[/b] If playtests are anything to go by, this results in somewhere [b]around 30-60 hours of content for completionists.[/b]
[*] It ALSO features a storyline exploring the Fisherman’s cosmic debt. To resolve this debt, you’ll need to [b]delve into the eldritch waters beneath the earth, learn arcane rituals, and slay the Leviathan[/b] before it consumes you.
[*] It’s [b]about 3-5 times larger than the demo?[/b] At least. There’s a LOT of content here, including [b]a fully-fleshed-out metaprogression system[/b] and [b]fourteen separate game-bending lures[/b] which augment builds and give access to special ultra-rare bounties.
[*] If the game launches well, I have plans for multiple free content expansions with [b]new maps, boats, weapons, and more![/b] The first content expansion will be called [b]WOMEN WANT ME.[/b]
[*] I will be [b]taking down the free demo when the game launches.[/b] This isn’t because I’m opposed to free demos, but because the demo will corrupt newer saves and completely erase 90% of your progress if you try to open it after opening the main game. There’s no way around this outside of completely remaking the demo, which I probably… do not have time to do.
[*] That being said, [b]if you played the demo, the game should remember your progress when you start the full game,[/b] and unlock anything you would’ve unlocked at your current level of progression!
[/list]
Thank you to everyone who played the demo, or wishlisted the game, or reached this page through other means! The game's evolved a lot since the demo a few months back, and I feel that it's turned into something really special. This game owes a lot to everyone who's provided feedback on the game in its various stages. I hope you enjoy the full experience!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3000120/FISH_FEAR_ME/
